<reason>PRO built a clean comparative frame from the start (the scene already exists; only the witness changes; the motion merely permits) and then progressively tightened it around CON's own admissions. CON's best material was the coverage/citywide-mortality point and the fixed-address magnet argument, both pointed and fairly answered by PRO (sites sit inside the open scene where deaths cluster; Insite's neighbourhood measure; dealers already have an address). CON's case suffered internal strain: it said police cannot hold a perimeter and no government has dislodged Cracolândia, then offered "enforced dispersal" and claimed scenes "scatter under pressure." PRO exploited that squarely, and its closing reframe of CON's outreach nurse as "a consumption site with the roof torn off" neutralized much of CON's alternative. CON's "the roof is the whole case" reply was a real distinction but came too late and did not resolve the dispersal contradiction. Both sides met the Q/A format; PRO's answers were more direct. PRO made the debate easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's [A4.4]-[A4.5] and [A5.1]-[A5.3]: stacking CON's concessions that police cannot hold a perimeter and no eviction has moved Cracolândia to show CON's implied dispersal alternative is impossible by its own account, leaving the same scene minus the person holding naloxone; then recasting CON's outreach nurse as the site's mechanism without the building.</best_rebuttal>
